genZNote: Cat bite, rapid red swelling within 24 hours — this is the organism your ER doctor is already thinking about.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Oral cavity and upper respiratory tract of healthy cats and dogs
habitat.hostAssociation: Normal oral flora of cats and dogs; opportunistic pathogen in humans following animal bites/scratches
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Primarily host-associated with domestic and wild animals
habitat.reservoir: Cats and dogs (very high prevalence in feline oral flora especially)

microscopy.stain: Gram stain; Wright/Giemsa may show bipolar ('safety pin') staining
microscopy.appearance: Small Gram-negative coccobacilli, sometimes bipolar staining

culture.growthCharacteristics: Facultative anaerobe; grows well on routine media, does not grow on MacConkey agar
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, gray, mucoid colonies with a characteristic musty/mushroom-like odor

identificationClues: Small Gram-negative coccobacillus, oxidase and indole positive
Does not grow on MacConkey agar — helpful differentiator from Enterobacteriaceae
Classic rapid-onset (within 24 hours) cellulitis/wound infection following a cat or dog bite or scratch

diseases: Cellulitis and wound infection following animal bites/scratches (especially cats, given their sharp, deeply penetrating teeth)
Septic arthritis or osteomyelitis if the bite penetrates a joint/bone
Respiratory tract infections in patients with underlying lung disease
virulenceFactors: Polysaccharide capsule — antiphagocytic in encapsulated strains
Rapid tissue invasion contributing to the classically fast onset of infection
clinicalImportance.transmission: Direct inoculation via animal bite or scratch, most classically from cats
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: The most common bacterial pathogen isolated from infected cat and dog bite wounds; rapid symptom onset (often within 24 hours) helps distinguish it clinically from other bite-wound pathogens with slower onset
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: A history of a cat or dog bite with rapid-onset cellulitis should prompt empiric coverage for P. multocida even before culture results return

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Oxidase positive, indole positive, no growth on MacConkey agar
examFacts.importantDisease: Cellulitis/wound infection after cat or dog bite
examFacts.importantTest: Culture on blood/chocolate agar (no growth on MacConkey); history of animal bite is a key clinical clue
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Classic rapid-onset (<24h) cellulitis following a cat or dog bite — faster onset than most other bite-wound pathogens
